findings.title: The SendGrid client used for cancellation is never authenticated
findings.body: This route only calls `sgMail.setApiKey`, but the new cancellation request at line 57 is made through the separate `@sendgrid/client` instance. `@sendgrid/mail` does not configure that client's authorization header, so the cancellation POST will be rejected by SendGrid and the error is only logged. Configure `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this route before calling `client.request`; otherwise cancelled reminders remain scheduled and are sent.

findings.title: A cancellation shortly before a reminder is due is not processed before the email sends
findings.body: Cancellation is now deferred exclusively to a cron job that runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled after a cron invocation and its scheduled reminder is due before the next invocation (for example, a reminder due in five minutes), no SendGrid cancellation is attempted before `sendAt`, so the reminder is still delivered. The one-hour query horizon does not solve this because it is only evaluated when cron next runs. Near-term reminders need an immediate/guaranteed cancellation path or a worker cadence that completes before their send time.

findings.title: Direct booking reschedules bypass the new durable cancellation flow
findings.body: The normal booking reschedule flow calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)`, which performs an immediate SendGrid cancellation and returns without setting `WorkflowReminder.cancelled`. This reintroduces the exact capped-pending-cancellation failure the PR is intended to avoid: when SendGrid rejects the immediate cancellation, the helper catches the error, the reminder stays `cancelled = null`, and the cron query will never retry it. Rescheduled bookings through this endpoint can therefore still send their old reminders; use the persisted `cancelled` path (or mark it for cron retry when the immediate call fails).

findings.title: One failed cancellation prevents all later reminders in the batch from being cancelled
findings.body: The entire loop is enclosed by one `try` block. If `client.request` fails for any reminder, execution exits the loop immediately and skips cancellation of every remaining reminder; it also skips the accumulated database deletes for prior successful requests. A permanently invalid or transiently failing batch can consequently leave other valid, imminent cancelled reminders untouched until a later run, and can repeatedly block them. Handle failures per reminder and persist successful cancellations independently so one bad SendGrid request cannot block the rest.
